roadmap.notes: Rigor profile thorough: pass model explicitly on every dispatch, the profile's agent_model for crafters and reviewer_model for reviewers. Every step is executed by a crafter; no step is orchestrator-only. A push is not a step: the orchestrator makes it after the step named in that step's implementation_notes. Sources: feature-delta.md. Its sections 'Maintainer decisions (2026-11-07)', 'Review revision' and 'What each slice must show' override earlier text, and rows A1 to E13 and C1 to C20 are named there. Those ids stay in the delta: no nWave scenario tag and no row id goes into a test title, comment or file. An untagged test is correct here. New tests carry no [Category("slice-...")]; moved rows keep the attributes they have. Comments follow CLAUDE.md: the why in plain words, no slice or Story id. NO PRODUCT CODE: guarantee 1, git diff --name-only <last green> HEAD -- Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/ prints nothing from this Story before each push. A deliberate break is made in the working tree, its output kept, then reverted, and it must compile. Lighthouse.Backend.Tests.csproj stays untouched; no ci*.yml edit, no new script (D-6469-17). A step needing either stops and reports. T5 adds no port: a scenario with no port stays at the host and the gap goes to #6508. No port row asserts a refusal by role. Mutation N/A in every slice: Stryker mutates the product and only test files change; the deliberate break stands in. The Hypothesis and state-delta mandate of the roadmap skill does not apply: docs/architecture/atdd-infrastructure-policy.md rules it out for this C# project. EVERY TEST RUN, class runs included, removes seven variables: env -u AzureDevOpsLighthouseIntegrationTestToken -u JiraLighthouseIntegrationTestToken -u JiraLighthouseRestrictedIntegrationTestToken -u JiraScopedTokenIntegrationTestToken -u ServiceNowLighthouseIntegrationTestToken -u LinearAPIKey -u AzureDevOpsLighthouseE2ETestToken. The same env -u list followed by env | grep -cE 'IntegrationTestToken|LinearAPIKey|AzureDevOpsLighthouseE2ETestToken' prints 0 first. This replaces the delta's five names and its grep, which cannot see the last two. FAST CYCLE: while working a step, run the named class, or Test-Fast.ps1 -NoBuild once it exists; contract, skeleton and host rows are outside the fast tier, so run them by class. One full run of the always-on clause A at each slice end and before each push, never more. A = Category!=Integration|(Category!=JiraIntegration&Category!=AdoIntegration&Category!=LinearIntegration&Category!=ServiceNowIntegration&Category!=GithubIntegration). No crafter runs an unfiltered or standard-filter dotnet test. Every restricted run states a nonzero count read from the TRX's Counters total, because dotnet test exits 0 on no match. RULES OF A LIST RUN, T6's: one at a time, never beside any other test run, ps -eo args | grep -cE '[t]esthost|[v]itest' prints 0, no build going, dotnet build-server shutdown first, Docker up, never repeated for a failed test, only for a crash that leaves a short TRX. Ids come from the TRX, never --list-tests, which hides a class move. Lists: P0 (01-01), PA (01-03), PB with the timer (02-07), P1 (04-01), P2 with the timer (05-05). PA and PB are additions to the delta's list of runs, for the slice-end rule. Each is compared with the one before, before any push: a line is accepted only if it is on the slice's id table, a test this Story added and named in the delta, or a foreign commit whose diff shows that exact test. An unexplained line stops the pushes. TRX and CSV stay out of git under evidence/, with count and sha256 in the delta. A kept TRX is searched for token shapes and real hosts first. CHECKS BEFORE EACH PUSH, part of the step before it: merge origin/main if clean, a conflict stops and reports, nothing is rebased; git diff --name-only <last green> HEAD through path-classifier.sh with each classify_* and a grep for ^.github/workflows/ci.*\.yml, any true means wait for a green run or tell the maintainer; guarantee 1; guarantee 2's tag grep; TestHostUseGuardTest by name with its count after the last merge. Each push waits for the one before to end, and read the result before pushing. After a push the orchestrator does the CI cross-check of the delta, CI CSV against CI CSV. At most two pushes here: push 1 after 04-01 (slices A to D, the guard and its text together), push 2 for E's first class, only after the maintainer's answer. test-time-budget.json is not edited: the Slice01 entry drops only under D-6469-20, needing 5 plain main runs after the move, and T9 does it if T5 ends first. New classes stay under the 34 s budget; one over it is split, never listed. A contract class name ends in WireContractTest, as T6's chain check fails on two classes sharing a simple name. File names for new shared parts are proposals; their internal shape is the crafter's. Measurement: the timing run of 2026-11-07 and the ranking addendum are the baseline. Rejected alternatives are in the delta: the host's container without HTTP, a base class for the helper, a wider port fixture.
